<translate>
<!--T:1-->
'''Tournaments''' are one-on-one ring fights against a ladder of NPC fighters, hosted by an NPC at a fixed arena. Enter alone or with your party, accept the rules, then fight your way up to the host's champion. Win the whole tournament for big TP rewards.
</translate>

<div class="dmz-cards">
{{Card|Fortuneteller Baba's Tournament|<translate><!--T:2--> A one-star gauntlet at Baba's Palace, ending with Kid Goku.</translate>}}
{{Card|Cell Games|<translate><!--T:3--> Cell's lethal bracket of Z Fighters, ending with Super Perfect Cell.</translate>}}
{{Card|World Martial Arts Tournament|<translate><!--T:78--> A four-star bracket on an ocean island, ending with the World Champion, Mr. Satan.</translate>}}
{{Card|Otherworld Tournament|<translate><!--T:4--> The afterlife's five-star bracket, ending with Gogeta.</translate>}}
</div>

<translate>
== The tournaments == <!--T:5-->
</translate>

<translate>
<!--T:28-->
* [[Special:MyLanguage/Cell|Cell]] talks to every player. His Evil alignment requirement (40 or less) only locks his '''Skills''' and '''Train''' as a master, not the Cell Games.
* To reach the Otherworld Tournament, talk to the [[Special:MyLanguage/Grand Kai|Grand Kai]] next to [[Special:MyLanguage/King Yemma|King Yemma]] and press '''Tournament'''. The [[Special:MyLanguage/Otherworld Tournament Announcer|Announcer]] can send you back.
* The [[Special:MyLanguage/World Martial Arts Tournament|World Martial Arts Tournament]] island generates once per world in the oceans. Find it with <code>/dmzlocate budokai_tenkaichi</code> or a [[Special:MyLanguage/Capsule Corp Assistant|Capsule Corp Assistant]] map, and sign up with the World Tournament Announcer.
* Qualifier fighters get '''8% stronger''' each round (Baba's fighters 10%).
</translate>

<translate>
== Formats == <!--T:29-->

<!--T:30-->
* '''Bracket''': you're seated in a knockout bracket filled with random NPC contenders. Winners climb the ladder; fights between two NPCs are decided automatically. After the qualifier rounds, the survivor faces the host's '''semi-finalist''', then (Otherworld and World Martial Arts Tournament only) a '''finalist''', then the '''champion'''. Only the semi-finalist, finalist and champion are known before you enter; the rest of the draw is revealed once everybody accepts the rules.
* '''Gauntlet''': you beat every fighter from left to right, then the semi-finalist and the champion.

<!--T:31-->
'''Lethal''' tournaments can kill you: a lost bout is a real death. '''Knockout''' tournaments end each bout at knockout and nobody dies.
</translate>

<translate>
== Entering == <!--T:32-->

<!--T:33-->
# Talk to the host and press '''Tournament''' to open the tournament screen, then '''Enter'''. You must be within 12 blocks of the host.
# If you're in a party, '''only the party leader''' can enter, and the whole party enters together. Nobody can join or be invited to the party until the tournament is over, and a member who leaves the party is disqualified.
# Every member gets the '''rules''' screen and has '''60 seconds''' to '''Accept''' or '''Decline''' (Decline asks for confirmation). Whoever declines, doesn't answer or logs out drops out; in a bracket, their seat goes to a random fighter. If nobody accepts, the tournament is called off.
# Only one run of each tournament can happen at a time. You can't enter while you're on cooldown or still entered in another tournament.
</translate>

<translate>
=== Bouts === <!--T:34-->

<!--T:35-->
* When your bout is next, the tournament screen opens and you have '''30 seconds''' to press '''Ready'''. Hover your opponent to study their stats and, once you have Bulma's '''Threat Database''' scan data, their ki attacks and combos. Miss the window and you're disqualified (your opponent advances).
* When everyone in the bout is ready, a 5-second preview plays, then you're teleported into the ring. Fighters stand frozen through a '''3-2-1''' countdown, then '''FIGHT!'''
* Only your opponent can hurt you and only you can hurt them. Anyone else who comes within '''15 blocks''' of the fighters is pushed out.
* Each bout has a time limit (Baba 5 minutes, Cell 7 minutes, Otherworld 8 minutes, World Martial Arts Tournament 7 minutes). A bout that runs out of time is void and fought again.
* Stay within '''60 blocks''' of the ring. If you walk away (or log out), you have '''15 seconds''' to come back, or you're out. Party members called into the tournament from elsewhere get '''60 seconds''' to reach the arena.
* Losing a bout knocks you out of the tournament and starts your re-entry cooldown.
</translate>

<translate>
=== Parties === <!--T:36-->

<!--T:37-->
* '''Bracket:''' each member has their own seat. If the draw puts two members against each other, they fight a PvP bout.
* '''Gauntlet:''' the party shares one ladder and takes the ring in turns. If the current fighter loses, another member steps in against the same opponent. When the champion falls, '''every member who accepted the rules''' gets the rewards.
</translate>

<translate>
=== Winning === <!--T:38-->

<!--T:39-->
The winner gets the TP and alignment rewards, fireworks and the victory music, and the cooldown starts again (by default the same length as the re-entry cooldown).
</translate>

<translate>
== The tournament screen == <!--T:40-->

<!--T:41-->
The screen shows the tournament name and difficulty stars, its format (Bracket or Gauntlet) and whether it's Lethal or Knockout, a status line, and your party members with their state (★ leader, ✓ accepted or ready, … pending, ✗ out, ⚔ fighting).

<!--T:42-->
* '''Rules view''': the numbered rules of this tournament, with '''Accept''' and '''Decline'''.
* '''Bracket view''': brackets are drawn as a vertical tree, where winners climb towards the champion's seat at the top; gauntlets are drawn left to right. Hover any fighter for details. Large brackets scroll.
* During the accept window and the preview, a card in the quest notice area of your [[Special:MyLanguage/HUD|HUD]] and big on-screen titles count down to the fight.
</translate>

<translate>
== Arena protection == <!--T:43-->

<!--T:44-->
The tournament arenas (Baba's Palace, the [[Special:MyLanguage/Cell Arena|Cell Arena]], the Otherworld Tournament grounds and the [[Special:MyLanguage/World Martial Arts Tournament|World Martial Arts Tournament]] island) can't be built in or broken by survival players unless the gamerule <code>allowBuildingInArenaStructures</code> is <code>true</code>. See [[Special:MyLanguage/Gamerules|Gamerules]].
</translate>

<translate>
== Commands == <!--T:45-->

<!--T:46-->
All <code>/dmztournament</code> subcommands require operator permission level 2. The tournament ids are <code>baba</code>, <code>cell</code>, <code>otherworld</code> and <code>budokai</code> (the World Martial Arts Tournament).
</translate>
{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:47--> Command</translate> !! <translate><!--T:48--> What it does</translate>
|-
| {{Command|/dmztournament cooldown clear &lt;players&gt; [tournament]}} || <translate><!--T:49--> Clears the players' cooldown for one tournament, or for all of them.</translate>
|-
| {{Command|/dmztournament ring &lt;tournament&gt;}} || <translate><!--T:50--> Stand where you want the ring centre (inside the arena structure) and run this: the position is saved into that tournament's <code>ring</code> offset.</translate>
|}

<translate>
== Configuration == <!--T:51-->

<!--T:52-->
Each tournament is one file in <code>config/dragonminez/tournaments/</code> named after its id (<code>baba.json</code>, <code>cell.json</code>, <code>otherworld.json</code>, <code>budokai.json</code>), generated with the defaults and version-updated like the other config files. Any other <code>.json</code> file in the folder is loaded too (files starting with <code>old_</code> are ignored), but only the four shipped ids have a host NPC. Reload with <code>/dmzreload config</code>.
</translate>

{{See also|Reloading and Updating Changes|How to JSON}}

<translate>
<!--T:76-->
Each fighter has <code>entityId</code> (an entity id, or <code>#tag</code> to draw a random member of an entity tag; the fighter is shown with that entity's own name), <code>health</code>, <code>meleeDamage</code>, <code>kiDamage</code>, <code>aiTier</code> (<code>1</code> Novice to <code>4</code> Expert), <code>perRoundScaling</code> (stats are multiplied by this value once per round already played) and <code>halo</code> (draws a halo on the fighter).
</translate>

<translate>
<!--T:77-->
A fighter drawn from a tag is always a character who isn't in the tournament yet: the semi-finalist, the finalist and the champion are resolved first, then the contenders with a fixed entity id, then the tag draws in list order, and the forms of a character (base, Super Saiyan and so on) count as one. A contender entry whose tag has no character left is skipped.

<!--T:85-->
Characters in the entity tag <code>#dragonminez:non_fighters</code> are never drawn from a tag, even if the tag lists them. By default these are [[Special:MyLanguage/Bulma|Bulma]] and the World Tournament Announcer, so neither can turn up as a contender.
</translate>
